name: Ottomanism
summary: Ottomanism, the Tanzimat-era state ideology (1839-1876), sought to bind the empire's Muslim and non-Muslim communities into one civic Ottoman nationality with equal rights and duties under the Sultan's dynasty. It paired legal equality, merit-based office, secured property and a constitution with an indivisible state, an Islamic state religion and the retention of communal religious privileges.
scope: The civic Ottomanism of the Tanzimat and the 1876 constitutional programme (Rescripts of 1839 and 1856, the 1876 Constitution, Midhat Pasha and the Young Ottomans), as a state doctrine. It excludes Hamidian pan-Islamism, Pan-Turkism and later Turkish nationalism, and only partly the Young Ottomans' distinct Islamic constitutionalism (noted as a split).
